Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. I pulled together an initial Mutual Action Plan (attached) that ties the evaluation milestones to a capacity reservation timeline so we can align procurement lead times with a realistic production launch. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm POC acceptance criteria and target POC completion date (your note earlier suggested mid-December).
- Confirm expected peak concurrency and sample token distribution (short/medium/long).
- Identify the procurement decision owner and any internal timeline constraints (legal/finance cycles).

Quick sketch of capacity options (included in capacity_model.xlsx):
- Option A (baseline): 4x H100 (80GB) — low-latency, minimal runway for POC/beta.
- Option B (standard): 8x H100 (80GB) — target for 1k concurrent users at steady state; preferred for go-live buffer.
- Option C (scale): 16x H100 or hybrid H100+A100 — for high-throughput clusters and rapid scaling.

Lead-time notes: H100 procurement typically shows 10–14 week lead; A100s are usually 6–8 weeks depending on vendor. If you need an earlier production date we can explore a staged tranche approach (deliver a smaller pool first, then add capacity).

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_20261103.pdf, capacity_model.xlsx

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
1) Complete POC & compliance checks — target Dec 15
2) Commercial sign-off and commit — target Jan 10
3) First tranche provisioning — ~week 8 after contract
4) Tranche 2 provisioning (if committed) — ~week 12 after contract

Can you confirm who should receive the formal MAP and whether procurement should be looped now? If useful I can also produce a calendar-friendly gantt for internal reviewers.

Thanks —

Appreciate the clear draft. A few notes from our side:

- POC/compliance: SOC 2 evidence and data residency details must be validated during the POC. Our target for internal POC acceptance is 15 Dec 2026.
- Procurement window: Our procurement calendar has an approval cycle that typically requires ~6 weeks after final commercial terms are submitted. That said, if we have a clear MAP and a confirmed SOW/Docusign link we can nudge the timeline.
- Staggered provisioning: Staggering works well — we prefer an initial small pool while the POC completes, then add the remaining capacity post-contract. Could you confirm what you can provide short-term to cover peak POC traffic (burst credits or hosted capacity)?

I’ve cc’d our procurement alias. Required next step from us is a commercial worksheet and an estimated commit-by date so we can calendar the financial approvals. Can you also surface any SOC 2 artifacts or pointer to your compliance pack?

Susan / Lauren —

Following up with sizing guidance based on the notes in the MAP and a few baseline assumptions. If you can share concrete telemetry (RPS, avg tokens per request, 99p latency targets) we’ll refine, but here’s a conservative starting point: 

Assumptions:
- Target steady-state concurrent sessions: ~1,000
- Avg sequence length: 800 tokens (mix of short and medium prompts)
- Target 99p latency per token: <= 120ms on H100

Suggested baseline configuration (throughput-first):
- 8 x H100 (80GB) pool — estimated token throughput ~500k tokens/min, supports our target concurrency with room for KV cache warmup.
- If you need lower single-request latency at high concurrency, consider moving to 12–16 H100 or mix in A100s for cost-flexible lanes.

Optimization levers:
- Quantization to int8/4 can yield 1.8–3x memory savings and ~1.5–2x throughput improvements for many encoder-decoder variants, subject to quality checks.
- Persistent KV cache for conversation workloads will reduce repeated prefix cost by up to 30–50% on long-running sessions.
- Batching policies: continuous batching at the routing layer; we can tune the batch window to hit latency SLOs while reducing token cost.

Lead-time guidance (procurement):
- H100 (new orders): 10–14 weeks typical from order to allocation on our Dedicated procurement channels.
- A100 (if available as an alternative): 6–8 weeks.

Given procurement lead times, a staggered tranche (4 H100 then +4 H100) gives you earlier capacity for POC while meeting longer-term throughput. I’ve updated capacity_model.xlsx with the throughput curves and a tranche schedule.

Happy to run a quick sizing call with your infra team if they can share a sample of request logs.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick reply. Below is a proposed MAP timeline that maps the evaluation milestones to tranche provisioning and commercial checkpoints. This is intended to give procurement the dates you asked for so internal approvals can be calendared.

Draft MAP timeline (dates are draft and can be shifted to match HelixHealth approval cycles):
- Nov 4–Dec 15: POC & compliance (SOC 2 artifact review) — Redwood provides hosted burst capacity + 30 days of credited usage to cover POC peaks.
- Jan 10: Commercial sign and commitment (target commit date — aligns with your approval window to get procurement moving).
- ~Week 8 post-contract (target mid-March): Provision tranche 1 (4x H100) — supports limited production/beta.
- ~Week 12 post-contract (target late-April): Provision tranche 2 (+4x H100) to reach 8x H100 baseline. Additional tranches available per agreement.

Action items for HelixHealth:
1) Confirm POC acceptance owner and SOC 2 contact for artifact exchange.
2) Provide decision authority name for procurement (Procurement lead email would be fine).
3) Indicate if HelixHealth wants us to present a short commercial worksheet for internal approval (we can produce a one-page summary).

I’ve attached SOW_draft.docx and included a DocuSign link in the related links field — if procurement can commit to having the SOW routed by Nov 18 we should be able to keep the Jan 10 commit target.

If you’re comfortable, please reply with the procurement contact and we’ll loop Ben (our Commercial lead) to draft the final worksheet/pricing.
